conclusion.label: Most likely cause
conclusion.text: Wear in the PBR-1 agitator gearbox (bearing or lubrication), with heat reaching the mechanical seal

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: PBR-1 agitator gearbox vibration against its own level over the first hour, at the same 48 rpm. The shaded gap is vibration the speed doesn't explain.

checks.label: Vibrating more than it did at the same speed
checks.value: 4.52 mm/s now against 1.95 mm/s over the first hour (+2.57 mm/s). Flag level is +0.5 mm/s.
checks.why: At a fixed speed a healthy gearbox vibrates at a fixed level. Extra vibration is coming from inside the drive.

checks.label: Rising steadily, and faster
checks.value: +0.84 mm/s per hour over the last 2 h, +0.90 mm/s per hour over the last hour. Largest 5-min step: 0.22 mm/s.
checks.why: Wear grows gradually and speeds up as damaged surfaces make more damage. A loose sensor or cable jumps instead.

checks.label: Sustained, not a passing spike
checks.value: Above +0.5 mm/s since 11:20 (2 h 45 min); above +0.25 mm/s since 10:45.
checks.why: Needs 30 min above the flag level, so a sampling spike can't raise it.

checks.label: Same speed all shift
checks.value: 47.8–48.2 rpm all day (setpoint about 48 rpm).
checks.why: Vibration rises with speed. With the speed unchanged, the process isn't asking more of the drive.

checks.label: Mechanical seal warming too
checks.value: 52.2 °C now against 44.0 °C over the first hour; more than +3 °C since 11:30.
checks.why: A separate sensor. Friction heat from a worn gearbox bearing travels down the shaft to the bottom-entry seal.

checks.label: Drawing a little more power
checks.value: 14.65 kW over the last 30 min against 14.27 kW in the first hour (+2.7 %), at the same speed.
checks.why: Friction in a worn drive costs power. A small rise at constant speed fits; a large one would point at the process (foam, viscosity).

checks.label: Other agitators unchanged
checks.value: SBR-1 Agitation and PBR-2 Agitation: within 0.03 mm/s of their own first hour.
checks.why: Drives in the same suite share power supply, floor and utilities. Only this one changed.

series.label: Steam saturation temperature at vessel pressure (steam on)

chart.title: What we see
chart.caption: PBR-3 drain temperature against the hottest the steam in the vessel could be at its measured pressure. In the first SIP the steam itself was too cool; in the repeat it wasn't.

checks.label: Cold point never reached 121.1 °C
checks.value: SIP steam on from 10:00. By 10:30 the vessel had stopped heating at 118.6 °C (peak 119.5 °C at 10:20) and the drain peaked at 115.5 °C at 10:40.
checks.why: The drain is the coldest point of the vessel. Every point has to reach 121.1 °C before the hold can start.

checks.label: CSG-1 header pressure sagged
checks.value: Clean steam header 3.00 bar(g) before the SIP, below 2.9 from 10:25, lowest 1.66 bar(g) at 10:40.
checks.why: PBR-3 takes its SIP steam from CSG-1 on the clean-steam layer. Lower header pressure means cooler steam at the vessel.

checks.label: Vessel pressure too low for 121 °C
checks.value: 0.92 bar(g) at 10:30: saturated steam at that pressure is 119.0 °C, under 121.1. At 1.11 bar(g), earlier in the same SIP, it was 121.9 °C.
checks.why: A separate sensor, and plain physics: steam can't be hotter than its saturation temperature, so no amount of waiting would have got the drain to 121.1 °C.

checks.label: Less steam delivered, not more used
checks.value: CSG-1 flow 991 kg/h early in the SIP, 625 kg/h at 10:30.
checks.why: A separate meter. If another user were stealing steam, header flow would have gone up as the pressure fell. It went down: the generator couldn't make it.

checks.label: CSG-1 level hunting
checks.value: Generator level swung over 25 points in the 30 min before 10:30, from 10:10; within 1.5 points earlier in the day.
checks.why: A generator whose feed pump is cavitating can't hold its level, and a hunting level means unsteady boil-off. It is the earliest sign at the generator.

checks.label: Next SIP passed once the header was back
checks.value: Header back above 2.9 bar(g) at 11:15. SIP from 11:40: drain ≥ 121.1 °C from 12:10 to 13:05 (55 min), F₀ about 78 min.
checks.why: Same vessel, same traps, same drain. Only the steam supply changed, and the SIP passed.

confidence.because: The growth clock is read from the seed's own VCD and the readiness from PBR-3's SIP record plus standard step times. It is arithmetic, not a diagnosis; the step times are the planning values, not a forecast.

action.text: Decide by 15:00 with MS&T and QA: apply the approved seed-hold contingency (drop SBR-1 to 33 °C to slow growth) or re-sequence media fill and QA review in parallel where the procedure allows. Do not let the seed pass 6.0 ×10⁶/mL without a decision.

PSIT11.impact: Short by about 1 h 23 min. The step times (6 h 30 min after SIP) are standard values; any step done in parallel shortens the gap.
